correctness.rationale: For every n>=2k+2 and k>=2 the operator identity T^k A=(I+...+T^(k-1))(I+T^(k+1)) is checked coefficientwise. Binary colours force balanced signs and even n. For odd k, odd order of the k+1 shift makes the second factor invertible and leaves an impossible zero sum of k signs; the 2-adic complementary construction has T^(k+1)x=-x. For even k, alternating signs work exactly on even n. A three-colour periodic word with a one- or two-letter splice satisfies all neighbourhood bounds by a two-arc count for k>=3 and eleven enumerated local five-letter windows for k=2. With gcd(n,k)=1 the first factor is invertible, yielding exactly 2^g labelled solutions if shift orbit length n/g is even. The standalone verifier supports, but does not replace, this general proof.

evidence: Kalinowski et al. prove Maj(C_n) for k=1, and broad degree-dependent upper bounds; their Section 2 does not state the C_n^k formula for k>=2.

The 2025 closed-neighbourhood paper includes sufficient parity constructions for circulants, potentially covering even-k sufficiency, but no necessity theorem for all consecutive-generator cycle powers.

Minyard--Sepanski (2026) require all three colours to occur equally often in each neighbourhood, forcing degrees divisible by three. Strong-majority asks only for every frequency to be at most half, so their hypotheses do not apply to the many powers with degree not divisible by three.

value.rationale: An infinite natural family of noncomplete 2k-regular graphs with unbounded k receives an exact sharp strong-majority number, exhibiting a genuine two-adic phase transition for every odd exponent. The uniform explicit three-colour construction shows the obstruction is the sole barrier to optimum two, while exact coprime labelled counts give additional structure. This is a full parameter classification motivated by a newly introduced invariant, not a tiny isolated case or an unmotivated enumeration.
